nodes.description: Biallelic STAT1 variants abolish (null alleles) or reduce (hypomorphic alleles) the amount of functional STAT1 protein, or leave a protein that is not tyrosine-phosphorylated after interferon stimulation. STAT1 is expressed in hematopoietic and non-hematopoietic cells, so the defect is present in leukocytes and in tissue cells such as fibroblasts and epithelium.

nodes.description: Patient blood cells do not respond to IFN-gamma with IL-12 production or HLA class II induction, so the IL-12/IFN-gamma loop that activates macrophages to kill intramacrophagic bacteria is broken. This is the same functional lesion as in the other forms of Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease.

evidence.reference_title: Human complete Stat-1 deficiency is associated with defective type I and II IFN responses in vitro but immunity to some low virulence viruses in vivo.
evidence.snippet: There was no response to IFN-gamma in terms of IL-12 production and HLA class II induction, accounting for vulnerability to BCG.

nodes.description: Exogenous type I interferon cannot protect patient cells against viral replication. Fibroblasts from patients remain permissive to HSV and vesicular stomatitis virus in the presence of IFN-alpha/beta. In vivo some low-virulence viruses are still cleared, so the clinical viral phenotype is concentrated on herpesviruses and live vaccine strains.

nodes.description: Seven of 32 patients developed hemophagocytic syndrome, triggered by HHV-6, live vaccines, suspected BCG or other infections. Because it occurs in patients who cannot respond to IFN-gamma, and NK cell degranulation was normal where tested, the cohort authors conclude it can develop independently of IFN-gamma-STAT1 immunity; its mechanism here is unknown.

nodes.description: Without STAT1, IFN-gamma cannot activate the gamma-activated factor (GAF, a STAT1 homodimer) or induce its target genes in monocytes and macrophages. In the partial form, activation is reduced rather than absent, or (K201N) impaired only in the first hour after stimulation.

evidence.reference_title: Impaired response to interferon-alpha/beta and lethal viral disease in human STAT1 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Neither IFN-alpha/beta nor IFN-gamma activated STAT1-containing transcription factors.

evidence.reference_title: A novel form of human STAT1 deficiency impairing early but not late responses to interferons.
evidence.snippet: Interestingly, the activation of γ-activating factor and ISGF3 was impaired only at early time points in the various cells from patient (within 1 hour of stimulation), whereas sustained impairment occurs in other known forms of complete and partial recessive STAT1 deficiency.

nodes.description: Recessive STAT1 deficiency also impairs IL-27 signaling. The original authors suggest this may add to the bacterial susceptibility; the contribution has not been separated from that of the IFN-gamma defect.

evidence.reference_title: A partial form of recessive STAT1 deficiency in humans.
evidence.snippet: We also show that recessive STAT1 deficiencies impaired the IL-27 and IFN-lambda1 signaling pathways, possibly contributing to the predisposition to bacterial and viral infections, respectively.

nodes.description: STAT1 is a subunit of ISGF3 (STAT1-STAT2-IRF9), the transcription factor that type I (IFN-alpha/beta) and type III (IFN-lambda) interferons activate to induce interferon-stimulated genes. Without STAT1, these interferons cannot induce an antiviral program in leukocytes or in non-hematopoietic cells.
